newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Jan natgas ends up, then gains more on AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Jan natgas ends up, then gains more on AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX January Henry Hub natgas futures ended sharply higher Wednesday in moderate trade, then rallied further on ACCESS after AGA reported an unexpectedly-large weekly gas stock draw, sources said.

January climbed 14.1 cents to close at $3.505 per million British thermal units, then rallied to $3.65 on ACCESS after a bullish AGA report. February settled 13.9 cents higher at $3.156. Most other months ended up by one-half to 5.6 cents.
"The market looks really strong and the AGA number was huge," said one East Coast trader, adding the steep backwardation in gas prices encouraged early withdrawals.
AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 104 bcf, well-above expectations in the 70-80 bcf range. Stocks are now 217 bcf, or 8.1 percent, below year-ago.
And with colder East Coast weather on the horizon, few expected prices to back off much near-term.
Technical traders still pegged January support at $3.10 and then at $3.04, a low from November 21. Resistance was now seen at the contract high of $3.68.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices gained more than 20 cents Wednesday to the $3.60s. Midcontinent pipes were up a similar amount to the $3.55-3.60 area. New York city gate gas notionally was talked in the $4.40 area, up about 20 cents.
The 12-month strip rose three cents to $2.471. NYMEX said 37,984 Hub contracts traded, down slightly from Tuesday's revised tally of 38,894.

NYMEX January Alberta natgas finished 15 cents higher at $1.75, with February closing up the same amount at a new high of $1.65. NYMEX said seven Alberta contracts traded versus no activity on Tuesday.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded, with January settling unchanged at $3.00.
On the KCBT, January ended 14 cents higher at $3.33, while deferreds closed 1.5 to 15 cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 0.1 cent to 17.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
